messages.subject: [statnet_help] Weighted Mixing Matrices?
messages.body_plain:
The mixing matrix is a really nice way to summarize data.  I have a  
directed network where my vertices are hospitals, my edges are the  
valued, directed number of transfers between the vertices, and vertex  
attributes are hospital  characteristics.  I would like to be able to  
produce the mixing matrix where the numbers in the table are total  
number of patients transfered between classes.  This would be the sum  
of the value of the edges directed between two classes.

I feel like if I was better at R I could recode the mixingmatrix  
function myself, but I am not there yet.

Can you offer any advice on how to do this?

Thanks in advance!
   Jack

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Re: custom curved exp terms
messages.body_plain:
Dear Statnet developers and users,

I've been developing custom ergm terms in Statnet, and I would like to  
implement some geometrically-weighted curved exponential terms.  This  
is a simple-enough task in the source code, but I'm stuck on  
interpreting the 'altkstar' example of an R source wrapper function:

InitErgmTerm.R: 152:    map <- function(x,n,...) {
InitErgmTerm.R: 153:      i <- 1:n
InitErgmTerm.R: 154:      x[1]*(x[2]*((1-1/x[2])^i + i) - 1)
InitErgmTerm.R: 155:    }

I gather that (i) indexes the various k-stars to be weighted  
(canonical parameters), but why is (x) --- which I assume corresponds  
to the geometric weighting factor lambda --- a tuple?  I've also been  
unable to find an equivalent mapping function in the literature, but  
I'll have another crack at it.

Thanks!

Best,
- Art.

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Re: bug in revisetheta0
messages.body_plain:
Dear Statnet developers and users,

I've come across a possible bug in ergm() when fitting the "altkstar"  
term with an arbitrary lambda value and 'fixed' = FALSE, which causes  
the process to abort before entering the MCMC run:

 > Error in newoverlap[j] = m$terms[[i]]$params[[j]] :
 >  nothing to replace with


It turns out that the theta0 names do not match the model term names.   
This can be fixed by replacing the following line:

InitErgmTerm.R: 169:	coef.names = paste("altkstar", lambda, sep="."),  
#coef.names: required

with
InitErgmTerm.R: 169:	coef.names = "altkstar",  #coef.names: required


Making this substitution restores normal functionality to fitting the  
altkstar term without a constraint on the lambda parameter.

Best,
- Art.
